products.name: Remote Help — Government (GCC High) Edition — Commercial
products.short_description: Deploy Microsoft Remote Help in a US sovereign cloud (GCC High) tenant — with the national-cloud availability, endpoints, and controls verified for government, not assumed from commercial.
products.description:
Deploy Microsoft Remote Help in a US sovereign cloud (GCC High) tenant — with the national-cloud availability, endpoints, and controls verified for government, not assumed from commercial.

Government tenants in GCC High cannot assume a commercial-cloud feature works the same way — or is even available. This solution deploys Remote Help for a US sovereign-cloud (GCC High) environment: it FIRST establishes, against current Microsoft documentation, whether and how Remote Help is offered in GCC High (and DoD), then deploys it with the correct national-cloud endpoints, licensing, and security/consent model for government — or, if a capability is not available in the sovereign cloud, states that plainly and gives the compliant alternative. It mirrors the commercial Remote Help solution's deployment discipline, adapted and re-verified for the sovereign cloud.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates.

What's inside

  • Sovereign-cloud availability FIRST — establish, per current Microsoft docs, whether/how Remote Help is available in GCC High (and DoD), before any build step; never assume commercial parity
  • National-cloud configuration — the correct GCC High endpoints, licensing, and tenant settings for Remote Help (all flagged verify-with-Microsoft)
  • Security & consent model for government — RBAC, session consent, and unattended-access posture as they apply in the sovereign cloud
  • Deploy + pilot — the app deployment, a pilot ring, and validation adapted to GCC High; name every object
  • Parity notes + gaps — a GCC-High-vs-commercial parity table, and the compliant alternative for any capability not available in the sovereign cloud

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

A Remote Help deployment done correctly for GCC High — availability and endpoints verified for the sovereign cloud rather than assumed from commercial, with honest parity notes and alternatives.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run scripts (read-only discovery/validation/reporting; remediation defaults to a safe preview):
    • RHELPG-Discovery.ps1 — GCC High/DoD read-only Remote Help posture: cloud context, feature presence, RBAC
    • RHELPG-Report.ps1 — export Remote Help deployment + RBAC role status to CSV (US Government tenant)
    • RHELPG-Set-RoleScope.ps1 — assign a Remote Help RBAC role/scope in a US Government tenant (DEFAULTS TO -WhatIf)
    • RHELPG-Test-Endpoints.ps1 — confirm the tenant resolves the US Gov national-cloud endpoints, not commercial
    • RHELPG-Validate.ps1 — PASS/FAIL readiness check for Remote Help on a US Government tenant

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all five PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
